body:
- [x] Analyze the issue: `aria-selected` in combobox uses `itemState.highlighted` instead of `itemState.selected`
- [x] Fix `aria-selected` in `combobox.connect.ts` to use `itemState.selected` (matching the select component pattern)
- [x] Add changeset changelog
- [x] Verify the fix with code review
- [x] Run CodeQL security check — no issues found

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>`Combobox`: `aria-selected` should be set on selected rather than highlighted items</issue_title>
> <issue_description>### Description
> 
> `aria-selected` should be set on the currently selected (i.e. "checked") options within an option list to enable assistive technologies such as screenreaders to grasp the current state of the input (i.e. selection). See for example Ariakit's combobox: https://ariakit.org/examples/combobox-multiple. When using a screenreader, for example, options with `aria-selected` set will be announced as "selected" (tested in Chrome with VoiceOver on macOS).
> 
> As opposed to that, Ark sets `aria-selected` on the currently highlighted (i.e. "focused") option, which is meaningless as it means that when navigating through the option list using the arrow keys, *all* items will be announced as selected and thus, the users has no way of grasping the actual selection.
> 
> ### Link to Reproduction (or Detailed Explanation)
> 
> https://ark-ui.com/docs/components/combobox#examples
> 
> ### Steps to Reproduce
> 
> 1. Open the dropdown of the combobox
> 2. Open your browser's inspector and navigate to markup of the options within the popover
> 3. Highlight different options using the mouse or error keys and observe how the attachment of `aria-selected` changes
> 
> ### Ark UI Version
> 
> 5.30.0
> 
> ### Framework
> 
> - [x] React
> - [ ] Solid
> - [ ] Vue
> - [ ] Svelte
> 
> ### Browser
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional Information
> 
> _No response_</issue_description>
> 
> <agent_instructions>Analysis of Issue #3772
> The issue reporter is correct. Here's my analysis:
> Current Zag Implementation
> There's an inconsistency in how Zag handles aria-selected:
> Combobox (combobox.connect.ts:397):
> "aria-selected": ariaAttr(itemState.highlighted),  // ❌ Uses highlight state
> Select (select.connect.ts:271):
> "aria-selected": itemState.selected,  // ✅ Uses selection state
> How Other Libraries Handle It
> Library	aria-selected based on
> base-ui	selected (actual selection)
> react-spectrum	isSelected (actual selection)
> Ariakit	Selected state (per issue reporter)
> Ark/Zag Combobox	highlighted (focus state)
> Ark/Zag Select	selected (correct)
> ARIA Specification Nuance
> The W3C APG example does show aria-selected="true" on the highlighted option for single-select comboboxes. However, this becomes problematic for multi-select scenarios because:
> Screen readers announce "selected" for every item as you navigate with arrow keys
> Users cannot distinguish already-selected items from the currently focused item
> Focus is already communicated via aria-activedescendant on the input
> Recommendation
> The fix should be in Zag's combobox machine. Change:
> // Current (incorrect for multi-select)"aria-selected": ariaAttr(itemState.highlighted),// Should be"aria-selected": ariaAttr(itemState.selected),
> This would:
> Make Combobox consistent with Select
> Align with base-ui and react-spectrum patterns
> Allow proper screen reader announcement of actual selections
> Still communicate highlight via data-highlighted and aria-activedescendant
> Verdict
> This is a legitimate accessibility bug. The current implementation makes multi-select comboboxes confusing for screen reader users because every highlighted item is announced as "selected" during keyboard navigation, while actually-selected items have no aria-selected indication.
> Do you want me to open an issue in the Zag repository or prepare a fix?</agent_instructions>

author: emmmmdeee
body:
### Motivation

- Provide durable, auditable recording of discovery "pivots" with an explicit, SQL-backed registry and correlation-aware logging.  
- Wire the default breach module registration to construct a fully configured, dependency-injected instance so bootstrapping produces a usable BreachModule without external setup.  
- Surface OpenTelemetry trace context into structured logs for improved cross-service correlation.

### Description

- Added `pkg/telemetry/pivot_registry.go` which implements a small telemetry package containing a `Logger` abstraction, `LogCorrelationDecorator` that injects OTel trace/span IDs, `ModuleLogger`, a `Clock` abstraction and `SystemClock`, and a `PivotRegistry` with `NewPivotRegistry`, `EnsureSchema`, and `RecordPivot` methods plus helper functions for statement construction and validation.  
- Updated `internal/module/bootstrap_registry.go` to replace direct calls to the breach constructor with `newDefaultBreachModule()` and added `breachClock`, `breachSleeper`, and `newDefaultBreachModule()` helpers that build a `modules.BreachModuleConfig` with an `http.Client`, default sources, and sensible timeouts.  
- Added `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace` dependency to `go.mod` to allow extraction of trace/span identifiers for log correlation.  
- All new APIs require explicit dependencies (context, DB, logger, clock) and return errors on failure paths; defaults that could hide failures (like schema apply) are opt-in via `PivotRegistryOptions`.

### Testing

- Ran `go get go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace@v1.24.0` to fetch the tracing dependency and it completed successfully.  
- Ran `go vet ./...` on the repository which reported failures due to existing redeclarations in `pkg/dashboard` (pre-existing conflicts unrelated to the telemetry and bootstrap changes), so vet did not complete cleanly.  
- Ran `go build ./...` which failed for the same redeclaration conflicts in `pkg/dashboard`, so a full build did not succeed in this environment.

body:
The `error-log-to-thread-please` reaction posts a reminder message but leaves the original error log in the channel. This adds a new action that reposts the original message to its thread, then deletes it from the channel to save space.

## Changes

- **New action handler**: `REPOST_TO_THREAD_AND_DELETE` in `lambda_function.py`
  - Retrieves original message content
  - Posts configurable message template to thread with original message quoted
  - Deletes message from channel (preserved in thread via repost)
  - Handles placeholders with channel-specific values and defaults
  - Escapes curly braces in user content to avoid format string conflicts

- **New reaction config**: `error-log-to-thread-and-delete` in `config.yaml`
  - Configurable response template with `{user_message}`, `{link}`, `{user}`, `{channel}` placeholders
  - Channel-specific links for course-related channels with default fallback

- **Tests**: 6 new test cases covering nominal flow and edge cases (missing message/user, placeholder matching failure, curly braces in content)

- **Documentation**: Updated README with new action type and reaction description

## Example Configuration

```yaml
- reaction: error-log-to-thread-and-delete
  type: REPOST_TO_THREAD_AND_DELETE
  placeholders:
    link:
      course-ml-zoomcamp: https://github.com/.../asking-questions.md
      default: https://datatalks.club/slack/guidelines.html
  message: |
    Removing the message from the channel to save space. Please move the error log to the thread.
    
    Follow <{link}|these recommendations> to make it easier to help you.
    
    Here's the original message:
    
    > {user_message}
```

The original `error-log-to-thread-please` reaction remains unchanged for backward compatibility.

author: sanketmuchhala
body:
## Summary
Refactored the portfolio from a vanilla Three.js implementation to a modern React Three Fiber architecture. This change improves code maintainability, component reusability, and developer experience while maintaining the immersive 3D bedroom portfolio experience.

## Key Changes

- **Framework Migration**: Converted from vanilla Three.js to React Three Fiber with TypeScript
  - Replaced `main.js` entry point with `src/main.tsx`
  - Simplified HTML to minimal React root structure
  - Removed manual DOM manipulation in favor of declarative React components

- **Component Architecture**: Decomposed monolithic 3D scene into modular, reusable components
  - `Room.tsx` - Walls, floor, ceiling, baseboards, window, and rugs
  - `Bed.tsx` - Bed frame, mattress, pillows, blanket, nightstand with lamp
  - `Desk.tsx` - Desk surface, monitors with animated screens, keyboard, mouse, chair with wheels
  - `Bookshelf.tsx` - Shelving unit with procedurally placed books and decorative items
  - `Plants.tsx` - Floor plants, small potted plants, and hanging plants with subtle animations
  - `Lighting.tsx` - Comprehensive lighting setup (ambient, directional, point lights)
  - `WallDecor.tsx` - Wall-mounted decorations (posters, shelves)
  - `Hotspots.tsx` - Interactive navigation points with hover effects and labels
  - `Scene.tsx` - Main scene orchestrator with OrbitControls and environment

- **Interactive Features**
  - Hotspots with animated bobbing and scaling on hover
  - Dynamic monitor screen glow with pulsing emissive intensity
  - Subtle plant rotation animations
  - Responsive cursor feedback and tooltip labels

- **Styling & Setup**
  - Inlined critical CSS in HTML head for faster initial render
  - SVG favicon for lightweight branding
  - Configured Vite for TypeScript/TSX support
  - Maintained warm, cohesive color palette across all components

## Implementation Details

- Used `useFrame` hook for animation loops (lighting pulses, plant rotations, hotspot animations)
- Leveraged `@react-three/drei` utilities (`OrbitControls`, `Environment`, `Html`) for enhanced functionality
- Implemented shadow mapping on key objects for depth perception
- Organized component positions and colors as constants for easy theming
- Maintained accessibility considerations with proper event handling and cursor feedback

## Benefits

- **Maintainability**: Each 3D element is now a self-contained, testable component
- **Scalability**: Easy to add new furniture, decorations, or interactive elements
- **Performance**: React's reconciliation and Three.js batching work together efficiently
- **Developer Experience**: Hot module reloading, TypeScript type safety, familiar React patterns

author: ssb-cgn
body:
# Pull Request

## Description
This PR adds consistent handling of time period information for figures.

The time period is now:
- extracted from the source table header (thead metadata)
- displayed under the chart title
- added to the rendered Highcharts data table when required

### Details
- Tables that already display the time period in the first header row (e.g. single-year tables like "2024")
  are left unchanged to avoid duplicate headers.
- The solution intentionally supports tables with a maximum of two header rows.
  More complex table headers are not suitable for figures and are therefore ignored.

### Additional improvement
Re-rendering of the Highcharts data table is now more robust.
This also fixes a formatting issue that previously occurred when toggling "Vis tabell".

Link to ticket: MIM-2196

body:
### Motivation
- Align the repository data layer with the `GamePlay.txt` design so configs reference consistent IDs and reward rules. 
- Fill missing config pieces (consumables, drop tables, schemas) so systems can interconnect without missing definitions. 

### Description
- Replace and centralize the generic data file with `src/Data/DataConfig.lua` that defines `Rules`, `Currency`, `Rarity`, `RandomStatPool`, `EquipmentSlots`, `AttackProfiles`, and `Schemas` used across systems. 
- Introduce concrete enemy definitions in `src/Data/ConfigForm.lua` for `Brainrot`, `EliteBrainrot`, and `BossBrainrot` including stats, drop table names and boss reward split rules. 
- Expand and normalize equipment in `src/Data/EquipmentConfig` and unify equipment IDs referenced by gacha/task/drop configs (e.g. `Sword_Common`, `Sword_Uncommon`, `DragonBlade`, `Armor_Rare`, `Helmet_Common`). 
- Update `src/Data/GachaConfig` to use rarity pools consistent with `DataConfig` and list items as `{ Id = ..., Type = ... }`, add consumable/gacha item mappings. 
- Convert growth/upgrade logic into data tables in `src/Data/HowtoGrowth` exporting `LevelExp`, `UpgradeCost`, and `PowerScoreWeights`. 
- Normalize runtime state and boss structures in `src/Data/PlayerState` and add `AutoFarm` fields. 
- Add `src/Data/ConsumableConfig.lua` and `src/Data/DropTableConfig.lua` providing potion definitions and enemy drop tables referenced by enemies/tasks/gacha. 
- Normalize `src/Data/TaskConfig` structure, add `PlayerTasks` sample state, and ensure reward `Item` IDs match equipment/consumable configs. 
- Files changed: 9 files modified/created, including two new files `ConsumableConfig.lua` and `DropTableConfig.lua`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this PR because the changes are configuration-only and require integration with runtime systems for validation.

author: gracjankubicki
body:
## Summary
This PR updates tool name resolution to support dynamic tool names without introducing a new public contract.

Name resolution order is now:
1. `$tool->name()` if the method exists
2. `class_basename($tool)` fallback

Fixes #41  
Supersedes #42

## Why
For external tool adapters (for example MCP/CRM), tool names are often runtime values such as `server.tool`, loaded from manifests or discovery. A method-based check supports that per-instance naming while keeping the API surface minimal.

## Why not `#[Name]` attribute?
`#[Name]` is class-level metadata, so it works well for static names only.

This change targets runtime/dynamic tool ecosystems where one adapter class may represent many tool names per instance. An attribute cannot model that per-instance variability without generating a separate class for each tool.

Using `method_exists($tool, 'name')` keeps backward compatibility and supports dynamic naming directly.

## Backward compatibility
No breaking changes. Existing tools without `name()` continue to work unchanged.

## Tests
- `NamedToolTest` verifies:
  - a tool class with `name()` uses explicit runtime name
  - a regular tool falls back to `class_basename`

author: kingkay000
body:
### Motivation

- HF Spaces was failing to boot because a runtime `APP_KEY` implementation in configuration caused file I/O / random key generation during config evaluation and `artisan` commands ran before a key was available. 
- Ensure the application has a stable encryption key available before any `artisan` command runs in constrained deployments where env vars might not be materialized into a `.env` file.

### Description

- Revert runtime key generation in `config/app.php` to use the standard `env('APP_KEY')` only, avoiding side-effects during config loading.
- Harden the container entrypoint `start.sh` by adding `set -e`, ensuring `.env` exists (copying from `.env.example` when missing), and generating a `base64:` prefixed 32-byte `APP_KEY` via `php -r 'echo "base64:".base64_encode(random_bytes(32));'` and persisting it into `.env` (using `sed -i` to replace or appending when absent) before running any `artisan` commands.
- Remove the previous `php artisan key:generate` call from the entrypoint so key creation is deterministic and occurs prior to artisan use.

### Testing

- Performed a shell syntax check with `bash -n start.sh`, which succeeded.

author: hhoikoo
body:
resolves #8639 (BA-4299)

## Overview

Fixes async resolver timing in `GQLMetricMiddleware` to measure actual execution time instead of near-zero coroutine creation time. Async resolvers are wrapped in an `_observe_coroutine()` helper that records duration after the coroutine is awaited, while preserving DataLoader batching.

## Problem Statement

- `GQLMetricMiddleware.resolve()` measured `time.perf_counter()` around `next(root, info, **args)`, which returns a coroutine instantly for async resolvers (~0ms)
- graphql-core awaits the coroutine later, outside the timing window
- All async resolver metrics reported near-zero duration (e.g., `0.000123s` for a 500ms+ query)
- Sync resolvers were unaffected

author: hhoikoo
body:
resolves #8638 (BA-4298)

## Overview

Adds sub-phase timing instrumentation to the GraphQL request handler, enabling identification of performance bottlenecks by breaking request processing into `gql_setup`, `gql_execute`, and `serialize` phases with individual Prometheus histogram metrics.

## Problem Statement

- Only total GraphQL request duration was tracked, making it impossible to identify which phase (setup, execution, serialization) was slow
- No visibility into configuration/validation overhead vs actual query execution time
- Performance debugging required guesswork rather than data-driven analysis

## Architecture

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant handler as handle_gql_graphene/legacy
    participant common as _handle_gql_common
    participant Schema as gql_schema.execute_async
    participant Metrics as GraphQLMetricObserver

    Client->>handler: POST /gql
    handler->>common: _handle_gql_common()
    Note over common: gql_setup phase starts
    common->>common: get_manager_status, get_resource_slots, validate, build GraphQueryContext
    common->>Metrics: observe_phase(gql_setup)
    Note over common: gql_execute phase starts
    common->>Schema: execute_async()
    Schema-->>common: ExecutionResult
    common->>Metrics: observe_phase(gql_execute)
    common-->>handler: ExecutionResult
    Note over handler: serialize phase starts
    handler->>handler: json_response()
    handler->>Metrics: observe_phase(serialize)
    handler-->>Client: HTTP Response
```

---

author: theoephraim
body:
Adds multi-line support for function calls, both in decorators and item values.

Big pain that this solves is very long lists of imported keys. see #217 

Supporting this in item values does break our previous goal of not breaking other .env parsers, but I think it may be worthwhile. If a specific user needs to maintain support for another env loader for some reason, they can just choose to not use multi-line fn call values. This should be relatively rare unless you start getting into very complicated composition of values and functions...

Follow up work here is
- support nested function calls within decorators
- support commenting out whole lines within a multi line fn call
- support trailing comments after a line within a multi-line fn call
- support same commenting within decorator multi-line fns

author: copilot
body:
JReleaser was failing with "project.version must not be blank" and generating duplicate changelog category titles due to conflicting configuration.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`**: Pass version via `JRELEASER_PROJECT_VERSION` environment variable from workflow input
- **`jreleaser.yml`**: Remove manual `categories` definitions—`preset: conventional-commits` already generates them

```yaml
# Before
- name: Run JReleaser
  env:
    JRELEASER_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# After
- name: Run JReleaser
  env:
    JRELEASER_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    JRELEASER_PROJECT_VERSION: ${{ inputs.releaseVersion }}
```

The preset handles category generation automatically; explicit definitions were redundant and causing title duplication.

## 目的

プロダクトビジョンを明確化し、戦略ドキュメント群を整合させる。

`.ai-agent/surveys/20260208-renewal-product-vision/` での対話的な検討を経て、product.md を中心にステアリングドキュメントを再構築した。

## 変更概要

### product.md（プロダクト概要）
- ミッション「インディーズメディア作品を楽しむ時間を作る」を明確化
- 最終ビジョンの3つの柱を定義（媒体の網羅性、感性パートナー、没入感をもたらす創造性）
- 市場課題「自分の感覚を言葉にして入力しなければ、欲しいコンテンツに辿り着けない」を言語化
- ビジネスモデル（LTV重視、ストレージ課金が主要利益源）を詳細化
- Phase 1〜4 の戦略ロードマップと背景を追加
- 「1%の的外れ」問題と著作権リスクの課題セクションを追加

### market.md（市場分析）
- product.md の新ビジョンに合わせて全面改訂
- ターゲット市場を「インディーズ作品のコレクター層」に再定義
- 競合マップを「AI × 受動的」の観点で再構築
- TagStudio を競合として追加

### plan.md（実装計画）
- product.md の Phase 1〜4 との対応関係を明示
- Phase 6以降の詳細計画を削除（product.md に統合）
- Phase 3（おすすめ機能拡充 = 感性マップ）を最優先として明記

### work.md（作業の進め方）
- スキル名の表記を修正（`/autodev:start-new-task` → `/autodev-start-new-task`）

### survey（検討記録）
- ビジョン刷新の対話的検討過程を `README.md` に記録
- 外部レビュー（辛口フィードバック）を `review.md` に記録

author: gaborbernat
body:
The rust dependency update job was only running `cargo update` which updates `Cargo.lock` within existing version constraints. This missed updates to git dependencies pinned to tags (like tombi) and didn't bump version constraints in `Cargo.toml` (like pyo3 0.26→0.28).

Now the rust job updates all dependency types: 🦀 git dependencies by fetching the latest release tag via GitHub API, `Cargo.toml` version constraints via `cargo-edit`'s `cargo upgrade --incompatible`, and finally `Cargo.lock` via `cargo update`.

### Motivation
- Bring the application up to Laravel 11 compatibility by updating framework and platform-level dependencies.
- Modernize the bootstrap and front controller code to use the Laravel 11 application configuration and request handling API.
- Align test tooling with current major versions so CI and local testing can run on modern PHPUnit and dev packages.

body:
## Summary
Implements comprehensive session reporting with quality scoring and detailed incident analysis. Report is automatically saved to file and displayed on exit.

## Changes
- Add `detailed_report` module with session analysis and scoring logic
- Generate reports with session score (Perfect/OK/Poor/Unacceptable/NoConnection)
- Calculate uptime percentages and absolute time for each connection state
- Track and display detailed incident timeline with timestamps and durations
- Always save detailed report to `/tmp/hale-summary-{timestamp}.txt`
- Display detailed report by default, short summary with `--short` flag
- Add `ROADMAP.md` documenting completed features and future plans

## Report Features
The detailed session report includes:
- **Session score** with explanation (Perfect/OK/Poor/Unacceptable/NoConnection)
- **Session metadata**: start/end times with timezone, duration, targets tested
- **Uptime statistics**: OK/Slow/Disconnected percentages and absolute time
- **Incident counts**: number of disconnections vs slow periods
- **Detailed issues table**: timestamp, status, duration, and average latency for each incident
- **Score legend**: definitions of each score level
- **Footer**: disclaimer and GitHub repository link

## Behavioral Changes
1. Always writes detailed report to `/tmp/hale-summary-{timestamp}.txt` (even with `--short`)
2. Displays detailed report on console by default
3. Displays short summary when `--short` flag is used
4. Respects `--silent` flag (no console output, but file still written)
5. Shows both log file and summary file paths on exit
6. Maintains existing log file behavior

#### 📝 Explanation and details


The optimized code achieves a **131x speedup** (13,073% faster) by fundamentally restructuring the algorithm to eliminate nested iteration. The original implementation uses a nested generator expression that results in O(n×m) complexity, where for each node it checks all edges. The optimized version reduces this to O(n+m) by pre-computing a set of source IDs.

**Key optimization techniques:**

1. **Set-based lookup instead of nested iteration**: The original code calls `all(e["source"] != n["id"] for e in edges)` for each node, which means for every node, it iterates through all edges. The optimized version builds `sources = {e["source"] for e in edges}` once upfront, creating a hash set that enables O(1) membership checks via `n["id"] not in sources`.

2. **Early return path for empty edges**: When there are no edges, the optimized code immediately returns the first node without any ID lookups, matching the original's lazy evaluation behavior while being more explicit and faster.

3. **Direct iteration over explicit loop**: Replacing the generator expression with a straightforward for-loop eliminates the overhead of generator machinery and makes the control flow more efficient.

**Performance across test cases:**

The optimization shows dramatic improvements across all scenarios:
- **Small graphs** (2-5 nodes): 71-129% faster

**Why this matters:**

This optimization is particularly valuable for graph algorithms that need to identify terminal nodes in flows or DAGs. author: liuxiaopai-ai
body:
## Summary

The file tree API (`/api/files`) and file preview API (`/api/files/preview`) have ineffective path safety checks that could allow reading arbitrary files on the host system.

## Problem

### `/api/files` (file tree)
```typescript
// Current code — always returns true (comparing a path to itself)
if (!isPathSafe(resolvedDir, resolvedDir)) { ... }
```

### `/api/files/preview` (file preview)
```typescript
// Current code — always returns true (a file is always inside its parent)
const dir = path.dirname(resolvedPath);
if (!isPathSafe(dir, resolvedPath)) { ... }
```

This means requests like `GET /api/files/preview?path=/etc/passwd` will succeed and return the file contents.

## Fix

- Added a `baseDir` query parameter to both APIs. The frontend can pass the session's `workingDirectory` as the trust boundary.
- When `baseDir` is provided, the requested path is validated to be within it using the existing `isPathSafe()` function.
- For `/api/files/preview` without `baseDir`, falls back to restricting access to the user's home directory (prevents reading system files like `/etc/passwd`).
- Backward compatible: existing callers without `baseDir` continue to work, with the home directory fallback providing a reasonable safety net.

## Security Note

CodePilot runs locally so the attack surface is limited, but proper validation prevents accidental exposure when the dev server is bound to non-localhost interfaces or accessed via browser extensions.

## Tests

Added 13 unit tests (`src/__tests__/unit/files-security.test.ts`) covering:
- ✅ Paths within project directory (allowed)
- ✅ Paths outside project directory (blocked)
- ✅ Path traversal via `../` (blocked)
- ✅ Directory prefix attacks (`/project` vs `/project-evil`) (blocked)
- ✅ Symlink escape attempts (blocked)
- ✅ System file access (`/etc/passwd`) (blocked)
- ✅ Edge cases (root path, same path)

All 13 tests pass:
```
# tests 13
# pass 13
# fail 0
```

Run with: `npx tsx --test src/__tests__/unit/files-security.test.ts`

> - Or there is an `import` statement inside a `try/except` block later in the function that shadows the module-level import
> 
> **Fix approach:** Search `sort_textures_thread` thoroughly for ANY `from pathlib import Path` or `Path =` assignment ANYWHERE in the function body (including in except/finally blocks, and including the `import traceback` and `from tkinter import messagebox` imports that appear in the except block around line 2248). > Tooltips throughout the application are not displaying. The `WidgetTooltip` class in `src/features/tutorial_system.py` exists and looks correct, but tooltips are likely being garbage collected because references aren't being stored. >

body:
This PR introduces Document DB capabilities to WatermelonDB.

**Key Features:**
1.  **JSON Column Type:** You can now define `type: 'json'` in your schema.
2.  **Generated Columns:** Support for `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) VIRTUAL` columns. This is crucial for **indexing specific paths** within a JSON document and creating efficient queries.
3.  **Indexing & FKs on JSON:** By combining JSON columns with Generated Columns, users can index deeply nested fields and even create Foreign Keys based on JSON data.
4.  **Full Text Search (FTS):** Instructions included on how to use FTS with JSON content via generated columns.
5.  **Documentation:** A complete rewrite of the `README.md` to document these new features.

**Implementation Details:**

body:
Implements client-side autocomplete to improve city search UX. Users can now select from 70+ pre-configured cities across Uzbekistan, Russia, Europe, Asia, and Americas with keyboard/mouse navigation.

### Changes

**HTML**
- Wrapped input in `autocomplete-container` for positioning context
- Added `autocomplete-list` div for dropdown rendering

**CSS**
- Dropdown with slideDown animation, gradient hover/active states, custom scrollbar
- `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` support for accessibility
- Mobile-responsive with proper z-indexing

**JavaScript**
- Pre-processed lowercase city array for O(1) case-insensitive filtering
- Keyboard navigation: Arrow keys, Enter, Escape
- Optimized click-outside handler (only checks when dropdown visible)
- Max 10 suggestions per query

### Implementation Details

```javascript
// Pre-processed for performance
const popularCitiesLower = popularCities.map(city => city.toLowerCase());

// Efficient filtering with early termination
function filterCities(input) {
    const searchText = input.toLowerCase().trim();
    const results = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < popularCities.length && results.length < 10; i++) {
        if (popularCitiesLower[i].includes(searchText)) {
            results.push(popularCities[i]);
        }
    }
    return results;
}
```

### Screenshots

**Russian input ("Мос" → "Москва")**

![Russian autocomplete](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fd51b66-cdfe-43f2-a854-107470e7bd8e)

- CodeQL: 0 vulnerabilities

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> # Добавить функциональность автодополнения для поиска городов
> 
> Необходимо улучшить UX сайта погоды, добавив автодополнение (autocomplete) при вводе названия города.
> 
> ## Требования:
> 
> ### 1. Создать список популярных городов
> - Добавить массив с популярными городами мира (50-100 городов)
> - Включить города из разных стран:
>   - Узбекистан: Ташкент, Самарканд, Бухара, Андижан, Наманган, Фергана, Карши, Нукус, Термез, Коканд
>   - Россия: Москва, Санкт-Петербург, Новосибирск, Екатеринбург, Казань, Нижний Новгород, Челябинск, Красноярск, Самара, Уфа
>   - Европа: Лондон, Париж, Берлин, Мадрид, Рим, Амстердам, Барселона, Вена, Прага, Варшава
>   - Азия: Токио, Сеул, Пекин, Шанхай, Дубай, Бангкок, Сингапур, Стамбул, Дели, Мумбаи
>   - Америка: Нью-Йорк, Лос-Анджелес, Чикаго, Майами, Торонто, Ванкувер, Мехико
>   - Другие: Сидней, Мельбурн, Кейптаун, Каир
> 
> ### 2. Реализовать автодополнение
> - При вводе текста в поле показывать dropdown с подходящими городами
> - Фильтровать города по введённому тексту (регистронезависимый поиск)
> - Поддерживать поиск как на русском, так и на английском
> - Показывать максимум 5-10 подсказок одновременно
> - Подсказки должны появляться после ввода минимум 1 символа
> 
> ### 3. Интерактивность
> - Возможность выбора города из списка кликом мыши
> - Навигация по подсказкам стрелками ↑↓ на клавиатуре
> - Выбор подсказки по нажатию Enter
> - Закрытие списка при клике вне области
> - Закрытие списка при нажатии Escape
> - Подсветка активного элемента при навигации стрелками
> 
> ### 4. HTML изменения (index.html)
> - Обернуть поле ввода в контейнер для автодополнения
> - Добавить div для отображения списка подсказок (autocomplete-list)
> - Сохранить существующую функциональность поиска
> - Обновить структуру для поддержки autocomplete
> 
> ### 5. CSS стилизация (style.css)
> - Красивый dropdown список под полем ввода
> - Плавная анимация появления/исчезновения списка
> - Hover эффект для подсказок
> - Активная подсветка при навигации клавиатурой (.active класс)
> - Адаптивный дизайн (работает на мобильных)
> - Стиль соответствует общему дизайну сайта
> - Скроллбар если подсказок много
> - z-index для корректного отображения поверх контента
> 
> ### 6. JavaScript логика (script.js)
> Добавить следующую функциональность:
> 
> - **Массив городов**: Создать массив `popularCities` с городами
> - **Функция showSuggestions(cities)**: Отображает список подсказок
> - **Функция filterCities(input)**: Фильтрует города по введённому тексту
> - **Event listener на input**: При вводе текста фильтровать и показывать подсказки
> - **Event listener на клик по подсказке**: Вставить выбранный город в поле
> - **Keyboard navigation**: 
>   - ArrowDown - переход к следующей подсказке
>   - ArrowUp - переход к предыдущей подсказке
>   - Enter - выбор активной подсказки
>   - Escape - закрытие списка
> - **Click outside**: Закрыть список при клике вне области
> - **Интеграция**: После выбора города можно сразу искать погоду
> - **Очистка**: Функция closeSuggestions() для скрытия списка
> 
> ### 7. Оптимизация
> - Не показывать подсказки если поле пустое
> - Скрывать список после выбора города
> - Максимум 8-10 подсказок одновременно
> - Быстрая работа без задержек
> 
> ## Технические детали:
> 
> - Сохранить всю существующую функциональность поиска через API
> - Автодополнение работает только как помощник для ввода названия
> - После выбора города - тот же API запрос как раньше
> - Код должен быть чистым с комментариями на русском
> - Поддержка кириллицы и латиницы в поиске
> - Регистронезависимый поиск (toLowerCase())
> - Использовать includes() для поиска подстроки
> 
> ## Пример работы:
> 
> ```
> Пользователь вводит: "Мос"
> ↓
> Показываются подсказки:
>   - Москва
>   
> Пользователь вводит: "Par"
> ↓
> Показываются подсказки:
>   - Париж
>   - Paris
>   
> Клик по подсказке → город вставляется в поле → Enter или кнопка → поиск погоды
> ```
> 
> ## Файлы для изменения:
> 
> 1. **index.html** - добавить контейнер для autocomplete
> 2. **style.css** - стили для dropdown списка
> 3. **script.js** - вся логика автодополнения
> 
> Результат: Удобный и быстрый способ выбора города с современным UX!
